hints: Focus on how buta-1,3-diene adds, the two outer carbons join to neighbours so only one C=C remains in the middle of the repeat unit.
Draw the 1,4-addition repeat as $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-}$ and notice the C=C can still show cis-trans isomerism.
Recall cis means the two continuing chain bonds lie on the same side of the double bond, giving a U-shaped bend.
walkthrough:
**Write the monomer**

Think of buta-1,3-diene simply as $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. In the normal 1,4-addition polymer, carbons 1 and 4 open up to join the chain.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{-CH}_2\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-}$$

**See what is left in the repeat unit**

Only the middle becomes a single C=C. So the repeat unit must contain two $\text{CH}_2$ groups and one $\text{CH=CH}$ group, not two C=C bonds and not a side chain vinyl group.

**Apply cis meaning**

Cis around $\text{C=C}$ means the two $\text{-CH}_2\text{-}$ chain continuations are on the same side of the double bond. That gives a bent U shape with both single bonds below the double bond, which is the cis-1,4 repeat unit.

options.A: Incorrect. This shows two C=C bonds retained in every four-carbon unit, as in $\text{-CH=CH-CH=CH-}$. Addition polymerisation of buta-1,3-diene breaks one pi bond at each end, so only one C=C should remain per 1,4 repeat unit.
options.B: Incorrect. This has the correct connectivity $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-}$ but the chain bonds are on opposite sides of the double bond. That is the trans-1,4 arrangement, not cis.
options.C: Correct. This shows $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-}$ with both $\text{-CH}_2\text{-}$ groups on the same side of the C=C, giving the characteristic cis bend. This is exactly cis-1,4-poly(buta-1,3-diene).
options.D: Incorrect. This shows a different connectivity with a pendant double bond, corresponding to 1,2-addition rather than 1,4-addition. The question asks for the 1,4 cis polymer where the double bond is in the backbone, not in a side chain.
